verses.text: Are we starting to recommend ourselves again? Do we need letters of recommendation to you or from you, like some people do?
You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts and known and read by everyone.
It's clear that you are a letter from Christ, delivered through our service. It wasn't written with ink but with the Spirit of the living God—not on stone tablets, but on human hearts.
This is the confidence we have through Christ before God.
It's not that we're qualified on our own to claim anything as coming from us. Our qualification comes from God.
He has qualified us to serve a new covenant—not a written code, but the Spirit. The written code brings death, but the Spirit gives life.
If the ministry that brought death, carved in letters on stone, came with glory—so much so that the Israelites couldn't look steadily at Moses' face because of its fading glory—
won't the ministry of the Spirit come with even greater glory?
If the ministry that brought condemnation had glory, the ministry that brings righteousness has far greater glory.
In fact, what once had glory has lost its glory in comparison with the glory that surpasses it.
If what was fading came with glory, how much greater is the glory of what lasts!
Since we have this hope, we speak with great boldness.
We're not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so the Israelites wouldn't see the end of what was fading away.
But their minds were closed. To this day, that same veil remains when the old covenant is read; it hasn't been removed, because it is taken away only in Christ.
Even today, whenever Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.
The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
All of us, with unveiled faces, reflect the Lord's glory and are being transformed into his image, from one degree of glory to another. This comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
